questions.question: What does "AI" stand for?
questions.note: The term has been used since the 1950s for machines that mimic human thinking.

questions.question: Who coined the term "artificial intelligence" in 1956?
questions.note: McCarthy proposed the 1956 Dartmouth workshop where the field got its name.

questions.question: In "ChatGPT", what does GPT stand for?
questions.note: It is "generative" because it creates text, and "pre-trained" on huge amounts of writing.

questions.question: Which company created ChatGPT?
questions.note: Microsoft is a big investor in OpenAI, but OpenAI built ChatGPT.

questions.question: The Turing Test checks whether...
questions.option_1: a computer can calculate faster than a human
questions.option_2: a machine's conversation is indistinguishable from a human's
questions.option_4: a robot can walk like a human
questions.note: Alan Turing proposed it in 1950, calling it the "imitation game".

questions.question: ChatGPT was released to the public in which year?
questions.note: November 30, 2022. It reached a million users in about five days.

questions.question: In 1997, IBM's Deep Blue defeated which world chess champion?
questions.note: The first computer to beat a reigning world champion in a full match.

questions.question: DeepMind's AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol in 2016 at which game?
questions.note: Go has far more possible positions than chess, so this was a landmark.

questions.question: IBM's Watson won which TV quiz show in 2011?
questions.option_2: Who Wants to Be a Millionaire
questions.note: It beat champions Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter.

questions.question: Who won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics for work on neural networks?
questions.note: Their work from the 1980s underpins modern machine learning.

questions.question: AlphaFold, whose creators shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, predicts what?
questions.note: Demis Hassabis and John Jumper of Google DeepMind, with David Baker.

questions.question: ELIZA, written in the 1960s at MIT, was an early example of what?
questions.note: ELIZA played a simple therapist; some users were convinced it understood them.

questions.question: In machine learning, a model mainly learns from...
questions.note: Instead of following hand-written rules, it finds patterns in examples.

questions.question: What is "training data"?
questions.option_1: The examples a model learns patterns from
questions.option_2: The electricity a data center uses
questions.note: Better and more varied training data usually means a better model.

questions.question: When an AI chatbot states something false with confidence, it is called...
questions.note: This is why important answers should be double-checked.

questions.question: The text you type into a chatbot is called a...
questions.note: "Prompt engineering" is the skill of writing these well.

questions.question: Neural networks are loosely inspired by...
questions.note: Layers of simple units, roughly like neurons, pass signals to each other.

questions.question: A large language model like ChatGPT works by predicting...
questions.option_1: the next piece of text (token) in a sequence
questions.note: It has learned which words tend to follow which, at massive scale.

questions.question: Google's AI chatbot is called...
questions.note: It was earlier called Bard.

questions.question: Claude is made by which company?
questions.note: Anthropic was founded by former OpenAI researchers.

questions.question: Microsoft's AI assistant in Windows and Office is called...
questions.note: Clippy was the famous 1990s Office helper; Copilot is its modern successor.

questions.question: Meta's AI model family is called...
questions.note: Meta releases Llama openly, so others can build on it.

questions.question: xAI's chatbot, built into X (Twitter), is called...
questions.note: The name comes from a sci-fi word meaning "to understand deeply".

questions.question: Which of these creates images from a text description?
questions.note: DALL·E is OpenAI's image generator; Midjourney and Stable Diffusion do the same.

questions.question: To get a better answer from a chatbot, you should...
questions.note: Say what you want, who it is for, and the format you prefer.

questions.question: A chatbot gives you a medical or legal answer. What should you do?
questions.option_1: Trust it fully; AI doesn't lie
questions.option_2: Verify it with a qualified professional or trusted source
questions.option_4: Assume AI is wrong about everything
questions.note: Chatbots can sound confident and still be wrong.

questions.question: Which of these should you avoid pasting into a public chatbot?
questions.note: Treat anything you type as potentially stored or seen by the provider.

questions.question: A "deepfake" is...
questions.option_2: a realistic fake audio or video of a real person
questions.note: Deepfakes are used in scams and misinformation.

questions.question: A caller who sounds exactly like your grandson asks you to urgently wire money. The safest first step?
questions.option_1: Send a small amount to test it
questions.option_2: Keep asking the caller personal questions
questions.option_3: Hang up and call your grandson back on his usual number
questions.note: Scammers can clone a voice from seconds of audio. Always call back on a known number.

questions.question: Which task is an AI chatbot genuinely good at?
questions.note: Writing, summarizing, translating and brainstorming are its strengths.

questions.question: CAPTCHA puzzles on websites exist to tell apart...
questions.note: CAPTCHA stands for "Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart".

questions.question: "AGI" stands for...
questions.note: AGI means AI as flexible as a human across most tasks; it does not exist yet.

questions.question: The 2017 paper "Attention Is All You Need" introduced which design behind today's chatbots?
questions.note: The "T" in GPT is the Transformer, invented by Google researchers.

questions.question: "Narrow AI" means AI that...
questions.option_2: is good at one specific task
questions.note: Every AI in use today is narrow AI, even the impressive ones.

questions.question: The first global AI Safety Summit in 2023 met at Bletchley Park in which country?
questions.note: Bletchley Park is where Alan Turing's team broke the Enigma code in WWII.

questions.question: Which everyday phone feature typically uses AI?
questions.note: Face unlock matches your face using a learned model.

questions.question: The computer HAL 9000 appears in which film?
questions.note: "I'm sorry, Dave. I'm afraid I can't do that." (1968)

questions.question: In the Terminator films, the AI that turns on humanity is called...
questions.note: Ultron is Marvel; Jarvis and Vision are Iron Man's helpers.

questions.question: The humanoid robot "Sophia" was built by which company?
questions.note: Sophia has appeared on talk shows and at the United Nations.

questions.question: DeepMind's AI learned to play Atari games like Breakout mainly by...
questions.option_3: playing thousands of games of trial and error
questions.note: It saw only the screen pixels and the score, like a human would.

questions.question: The word "robot" comes from a 1920 play by which writer?
questions.note: From the Czech word "robota", meaning forced labor.

questions.question: Which sci-fi author created the famous "Three Laws of Robotics"?
questions.note: First law: a robot may not injure a human being.

questions.question: In simple terms, what is "machine learning"?
questions.option_1: Writing rules for every situation by hand
questions.option_2: Systems that learn patterns from data instead of following fixed rules
questions.note: Machine learning lets computers improve from examples rather than explicit instructions.

questions.question: What does "LLM" stand for in AI?
questions.note: LLMs like GPT are trained on huge amounts of text.

questions.question: When a chatbot reads your message, it breaks the text into pieces called...
questions.note: A token is a small chunk of text - often part of a word - that the model processes.

questions.question: What is "fine-tuning" an AI model?
questions.option_2: Extra training on specific data to adapt it for a task
questions.option_4: Compressing it to run on phones
questions.note: Fine-tuning takes a pre-trained model and trains it further for a narrower purpose.

questions.question: A "multimodal" AI model can...
questions.option_1: Run on many computers at once
questions.option_2: Work with more than one kind of input, like text and images
questions.note: Multimodal models handle text, images, audio or video together.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of "generative AI"?
questions.option_1: A spam filter that sorts email
questions.option_2: A chatbot that writes a brand-new poem for you
questions.note: Generative AI creates new content - text, images, music, video - instead of only classifying data.

questions.question: The 1956 Dartmouth workshop is remembered as the birth of which field?
questions.note: The term "artificial intelligence" was used for this 1956 summer workshop at Dartmouth College.

questions.question: Apple introduced which voice assistant with the iPhone 4S in 2011?
questions.note: Siri debuted as an iPhone 4S feature in October 2011.

questions.question: Which neural network's 2012 ImageNet victory kicked off the modern deep-learning boom?
questions.note: AlexNet won the 2012 ImageNet competition by a huge margin, sparking the deep learning era.

questions.question: OpenAI's GPT-3, released in 2020, drew attention mainly for...
questions.option_2: Its huge scale of 175 billion parameters
questions.note: GPT-3's 175 billion parameters made it far larger than earlier language models.

questions.question: DeepMind's AlphaStar reached Grandmaster level in 2019 at which video game?
questions.note: AlphaStar was rated Grandmaster in StarCraft II, above 99.8% of human players.

questions.question: Which Chinese AI lab's "R1" model made global headlines in January 2025 for strong reasoning at low cost?
questions.note: DeepSeek's R1 reasoning model triggered a major market reaction in January 2025.

questions.question: In a neural network, what are "parameters"?
questions.option_2: The internal numbers (weights) the model learns during training
questions.option_4: The list of websites it can visit
questions.note: Large models have billions of learned parameters.

questions.question: What is a chatbot's "context window"?
questions.option_1: The app window on your screen
questions.option_2: How much text the model can take into account at once
questions.option_3: The time of day it works
questions.note: A bigger context window lets a model consider longer documents and conversations.

questions.question: "Reinforcement learning from human feedback" (RLHF) trains a model using...
questions.note: RLHF uses people's preferences to make AI answers more helpful and safer.

questions.question: Image generators like Stable Diffusion work by...
questions.option_1: Cutting and pasting photos from the web
questions.option_2: Starting from noise and gradually forming an image
questions.note: Diffusion models learn to remove noise step by step until an image appears.

questions.question: What is "overfitting" in machine learning?
questions.option_1: When a model memorizes its training data but fails on new data
questions.option_2: When a model is too small
questions.note: An overfit model does great on data it has seen and poorly on fresh examples.

questions.question: In AI, an "embedding" is...
questions.option_2: A numeric vector that captures the meaning of text or other data
questions.note: Embeddings turn words and images into numbers that capture similarity of meaning.

questions.question: Perplexity is best known as an AI-powered...
questions.note: Perplexity answers questions with cited sources using AI.

questions.question: Which AI tool is built into GitHub to suggest code as developers type?
questions.note: GitHub Copilot, made with OpenAI, autocompletes code inside the editor.

questions.question: OpenAI's Sora generates what from a text description?
questions.note: Sora is OpenAI's text-to-video model, announced in 2024.

questions.question: ElevenLabs is best known for AI that creates realistic...
questions.note: ElevenLabs specializes in AI voice generation and text-to-speech.

questions.question: Google's NotebookLM can turn your documents into...
questions.option_2: An audio conversation, like a podcast
questions.note: NotebookLM's Audio Overview feature makes a podcast-style discussion from your sources.

questions.question: DeepL is a popular AI tool mainly for...
questions.note: DeepL is known for high-quality machine translation.

questions.question: A chatbot gives you a link to a research paper. Before citing it, you should...
questions.option_1: Trust it - AI does not make mistakes
questions.option_2: Check that the paper actually exists
questions.note: AI chatbots can invent realistic-looking references that do not exist.

questions.question: An "AI detector" claims a student's essay was written by AI. You should treat that verdict as...
questions.option_2: Unreliable - detectors can be wrong both ways
questions.note: OpenAI itself shut down its AI-writing detector in 2023 for low accuracy.

questions.question: Why do many companies ban staff from pasting confidential data into public chatbots?
questions.option_2: The data could leak or be stored outside the company
questions.note: Samsung banned staff use of ChatGPT and similar tools after an internal data leak in 2023.

questions.question: For questions about today's weather or breaking news, a chatbot without live internet access may...
questions.option_2: Give outdated answers - check a live source
questions.note: Training data stops at a cut-off date, so models can miss recent events unless they search the web.

questions.question: Which habit gets you better answers from an AI chatbot?
questions.option_2: Giving clear context, audience and format in your prompt
questions.note: Specific prompts with context and instructions produce better results.

questions.question: Before acting on an AI chatbot's summary of a long legal or financial document, you should...
questions.option_2: Spot-check key details against the original document
questions.note: Summaries can miss or misstate details; important decisions need the original text.

questions.question: The European Union's landmark law regulating AI is called...
questions.note: The EU AI Act entered into force in August 2024 - the first major AI law of its kind.

questions.question: The 2025 AI Action Summit, where countries discussed AI governance, was held in which city?
questions.note: The AI Action Summit took place in Paris in February 2025.

questions.question: In AI discussions, "the singularity" refers to...
questions.option_2: A hypothetical point when AI surpasses human intelligence
questions.note: The idea is associated with writers like Vernor Vinge and Ray Kurzweil.

questions.question: The 2018 Turing Award went to Hinton, LeCun and Bengio for breakthroughs in...
questions.note: The trio's deep learning work underpins much of modern AI.

questions.question: The US Copyright Office has said that works created entirely by AI, without human authorship...
questions.option_1: Can be copyrighted by the AI
questions.note: Its 2023 guidance says copyright requires human authorship.

questions.question: India's national program to boost AI computing, startups and research is called...
questions.note: The IndiaAI Mission was approved in March 2024 with an outlay of Rs 10,372 crore.

questions.question: In the 2013 film "Her", the character Samantha is...
questions.option_2: An AI operating system the hero falls in love with
questions.note: Her won the Oscar for Best Original Screenplay.

questions.question: The four-legged robot "Spot" is made by which company?
questions.note: Spot is Boston Dynamics' agile robot dog.

questions.question: In Star Wars, which golden droid is "fluent in over six million forms of communication"?
questions.note: C-3PO is a protocol droid built, in the story, by Anakin Skywalker.

questions.question: The 2022 horror film "M3GAN" is about...
questions.option_1: A lifelike AI doll that becomes dangerous
questions.note: M3GAN's creepy dancing robot doll became an internet meme before release.

questions.question: The original American female voice of Apple's Siri belongs to which voice actress?
questions.note: Susan Bennett revealed in 2013 that her recordings became Siri's original US voice.

questions.question: Baymax, the inflatable healthcare robot, appears in which animated film?
questions.note: Baymax won hearts in Disney's Big Hero 6 (2014).
